Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 51, verse 1–14:

Tafsir of Surat adh-Dhariyat

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

* *

Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj narrated from Simak, from Khalid ibn 'Ar'arah, that he heard 'Ali, and also Shu'bah, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Abu at-Tufayl, who heard 'Ali. It is also established through more than one chain from the Commander of the Faithful, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, that he ascended the pulpit of Kufa and said: "Do not ask me about any verse in the Book of Allah, or any Sunnah from the Messenger of Allah, except that I will inform you of it." Then Ibn al-Kawwa' stood up and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, what is the meaning of His statement, the Exalted: ﴿By those [winds] that scatter dust,﴾?" He said: "The wind." [He said:] "﴿And those that carry a load,﴾?" He said: "The clouds." [He said:] "﴿And those that glide with ease,﴾?" He said: "The ships." [He said:] "﴿And those that distribute by command,﴾?" He said: "The angels." (Related by at-Tabari in his tafsir (26/115) from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah.)

A hadith raised to the Prophet has been related concerning this, and al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ibrahim ibn Hani' narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sallam al-'Attar narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Sabrah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Subay' at-Tamimi came to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, inform me about ﴿those [winds] that scatter dust﴾?" He said: "They are the winds, and were it not that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say it, I would not have said it." He said: "Then inform me about ﴿those that distribute by command﴾." He said: "They are the angels, and were it not that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say it, I would not have said it." He said: "Then inform me about ﴿those that glide with ease﴾." He said: "They are the ships, and were it not that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say it, I would not have said it." Then he ordered that he be struck one hundred times and placed in a house. When he recovered, he called for him and struck him another hundred times, and had him carried on a saddle, and wrote to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari: "Prevent the people from sitting with him." He remained so until he came to Abu Musa, and swore by the strongest oaths that he found in himself nothing of what he had found before. Abu Musa wrote about this to 'Umar, and 'Umar wrote: "I do not think he is other than truthful, so let him mix with the people."

Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Sabrah is weak (layyin), and Sa'id ibn Sallam is not among the people of hadith. (Musnad al-Bazzar no. 2259, Kashf al-Astar; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/112): "In it is Abu Bakr ibn Abi Sabrah, who is abandoned (matruk).")

I say: This hadith is weak in its being raised, and the closest that can be said of it is that it is halted upon 'Umar, for the story of Subay' ibn 'Asal is well known with 'Umar. He struck him only because it became apparent to him from his manner of questioning that he was being contentious and obstinate. And Allah knows best.

Al-Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir mentioned this story at length in the biography of Subay'. (Tarikh Dimashq (8/230), manuscript section.) Thus it was interpreted by Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, as-Suddi, and others. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim did not relate anything other than this.

It has been said that what is meant by "those [winds] that scatter" is the wind, as has passed, and by "those that carry a load" are the clouds, as has passed, because they carry the water, as Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl said:

"I have submitted myself to Him to whom the cloud submits, bearing sweet, pure water."

(The verse is in Ibn Hisham's Sirah (1/231).)

As for "those that glide with ease," the well-known view of the majority, as has passed, is that they are the ships, running easily and smoothly upon the water. Some said: they are the stars, moving with ease in their orbits, so that this is an ascent from the lower to the higher, what is above them: the winds are above which are the clouds, and the stars are above that, and "those that distribute by command," the angels, are above that, descending with the commands of Allah, both the legislative and the cosmic. This is an oath by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, concerning the occurrence of the Return; therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, what you are promised is true,﴾ that is, a true report, ﴿and indeed, the Recompense is to occur,﴾ that is, the Reckoning, ﴿will surely happen,﴾ that is, it will certainly take place without doubt.

Then He said: ﴿By the sky having cosmic paths.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "Possessor of splendor, beauty, goodness, and evenness." Likewise said Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Malik, Abu Salih, as-Suddi, Qatadah, 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, ar-Rabi' ibn Anas, and others.

Ad-Dahhak and al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, and others, said: like the rippling of water, sand, and crops when the wind strikes them, so that some of it weaves into others in lines, and that is the hubuk.

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, from a man among the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "Indeed, after you is the lying misleader, and indeed his head is behind him, hubuk hubuk," meaning by hubuk: the curling. (Tafsir al-Tabari (26/118); Ahmad in his Musnad (5/410) through the route of Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah.)

And from Abu Salih: ﴿dhat al-hubuk﴾ means: the strength. Khusayf said: ﴿dhat al-hubuk﴾ means: possessor of smoothness.

Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿dhat al-hubuk﴾ means: adorned with stars.

Qatadah said, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah, from 'Amr al-Bikali, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr: ﴿And the sky of hubuk﴾ means: the seventh sky.

It seems, and Allah knows best, that he meant by this the sky in which are the fixed stars, which according to many astronomers is the eighth sphere above the seventh, and Allah knows best. All these sayings return to one thing, which is beauty and splendor, as Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said, for it is, by its beauty, elevated, transparent, dense, firm in construction, wide in its expanses, graceful in its splendor, crowned with fixed and wandering stars, adorned with the sun, the moon, and the brilliant planets.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, you are in a contradictory saying﴾ means: indeed you, O polytheists who deny the messengers, are in a saying that is contradictory, confused, not coherent and not consistent.

Qatadah said: "Indeed you are in a contradictory saying," meaning: between one who believes in the Qur'an and one who denies it.

﴿Turned away from it is whoever is turned away﴾ means: it is only promoted to one who is astray within himself, for it is a false saying that only those who follow it and go astray through it accept, and turned away from it is whoever is misled, astray, heedless, without understanding, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship, you cannot lead astray [against Him] except one who will burn in Hellfire.﴾ [As-Saffat: 161–163.]

Ibn 'Abbas and as-Suddi said: ﴿Turned away from it is whoever is turned away﴾: whoever has gone astray is led astray from it. Mujahid said: ﴿Turned away from it is whoever is turned away﴾ means: he is turned away from it who is made to turn away. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: whoever denied this Qur'an is turned away from it.

* *

His saying: ﴿Destroyed are the falsifiers﴾. Mujahid said: "the liars." He said: and it is like the one in 'Abasa: ﴿Destroyed is man, how disbelieving he is!﴾ [Abasa: 17], and "the falsifiers" are those who say, "We will not be resurrected," and are not certain.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Destroyed are the falsifiers﴾ means: cursed are the doubters.

Thus Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say in his sermons: "The doubters are ruined." Qatadah said: "The falsifiers are the people of heedlessness and speculation."

* *

His saying: ﴿Who are in confusion, heedless﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and others said: heedless and playful in disbelief and doubt.

﴿They ask, "When is the Day of Recompense?"﴾ They only say this in denial, obstinacy, doubt, and considering it far-fetched. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The Day they will be tried over the Fire.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, and others said: ﴿yuftanun﴾ means: they will be punished. Mujahid said: as gold is tested over the fire.

Another group, like Mujahid also, and 'Ikrimah, Ibrahim an-Nakha'i, Zayd ibn Aslam, and Sufyan ath-Thawri said: ﴿yuftanun﴾ means: they will be burned.

﴿Taste your trial﴾: Mujahid said: your burning. Others said: your punishment. ﴿This is what you used to seek to hasten﴾: meaning, it is said to them this as rebuke, reproach, belittling, and humiliation.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 51, verses 15–23 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about the God-fearing (al-muttaqun): on the Day of their return, they will be in gardens and springs, in contrast to what those wretched ones will face of punishment, torment, burning, and shackles.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿taking what their Lord has given them﴾: Ibn Jarir said: that is, acting upon what Allah has given them of the obligations (al-fara'id). ﴿Indeed, they were before that doers of good﴾: that is, before the obligations were prescribed for them. They were also doers of good in their deeds.

Then he (Ibn Jarir) narrated from Ibn Humayd, from Mihran, from Sufyan, from Abu 'Umar, from Muslim al-Batin, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying, ﴿taking what their Lord has given them﴾, that he said: "From the obligations." ﴿Indeed, they were before that doers of good﴾: "Before the obligations, they used to act." This chain is weak, and it is not authentically transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas. 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it from Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham, from Sufyan, from Abu 'Umar al-Bazzar, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, and he mentioned it. What Ibn Jarir explained it by is open to question, because His saying, ﴿taking﴾, is a circumstantial clause (hal) relating to His saying, ﴿in gardens and springs﴾. So the God-fearing, while being in the gardens and springs, are taking what their Lord has given them, that is, of bliss, joy, and delight.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Indeed, they were before that﴾, that is, in the worldly abode, ﴿doers of good﴾, like His saying: ﴿Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you did in the days past﴾ [al-Haqqah: 24]. Then He, exalted is He, explained their good conduct in deeds, saying: ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾. The commentators differed about this on two views:

The first: that "ma" is negating, its meaning being: they used to sleep little of the night, not sleeping it at all. Ibn 'Abbas said: No night passed over them without their taking some of it, even if only a little. Qatadah said, narrating from Mutarrif ibn 'Abdullah: Few were the nights that came upon them in which they did not pray to Allah, exalted is He, either at its beginning or at its middle. Mujahid said: They rarely slept a whole night until morning without performing tahajjud (night prayer). Qatadah also said likewise. Anas ibn Malik and Abu al-'Aliyah said: They used to pray between Maghrib and 'Isha'. Abu Ja'far al-Baqir said: They did not sleep until they had prayed 'Atamah (the night prayer of 'Isha').

The second view: that "ma" is verbal-masdar (masdariyyah), its meaning being: they used to sleep little of the night, their sleeping and their resting. This is the view Ibn Jarir chose. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: they endured the standing of the night, so they did not sleep of the night except a little, and they were energetic, extending it until the pre-dawn, until seeking forgiveness was at dawn. Qatadah said: al-Ahnaf ibn Qays said: ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: they did not sleep except a little, then he would say: "I am not among the people of this verse." Al-Hasan al-Basri said: al-Ahnaf ibn Qays used to say: "I presented my deeds to the deeds of the people of Paradise, and behold, they are a people who have far surpassed us, for we do not reach their deeds: ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night.﴾ And I presented my deeds to the deeds of the people of Hellfire, and behold, they are a people with no good in them, who deny the Book of Allah and the messengers of Allah, who deny resurrection after death. So I found that the best of us in standing are a people who mixed righteous deeds with others that were evil."

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: A man from Banu Tamim said to my father: "O Abu Usamah, here is a description I do not find among us. Allah mentioned a people and said: ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾, and by Allah, we stand but little of the night." My father said to him: "Blessed is the one who sleeps when he is drowsy, and fears Allah when he awakens."

'Abdullah ibn Salam said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in Madinah, the people rushed to him, and I was among those who rushed. When I saw his face, I knew that his face was not the face of a liar. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: "For whom are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "For the one who speaks gently, feeds food, and spends the night standing for Allah while people are asleep." [al-Musnad (2/173). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/165): "In it is Ibn Lahi'ah, and his hadith is good, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy." Perhaps al-Haythami's grading of Ibn Lahi'ah's hadith as good is because it has been supported: it is supported by 'Abdullah ibn Wahb, whose narration from Ibn Lahi'ah is sound, narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir no. (103), the missing volume.]

Ma'mar said regarding His saying, ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: al-Zuhri and al-Hasan used to say: "They used to pray much of the night."

Ibn 'Abbas and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾: they did not sleep.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿Indeed, they were before that doers of good. They used to sleep but little﴾, then he began: ﴿of the night, they would sleep but little, and in the hours before dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾.

* *

As for His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿and in the hours before dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾. Mujahid and others said: "They would pray." Others said: "They stood the night and delayed seeking forgiveness until the pre-dawn hours," as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿and those who seek forgiveness in the hours before dawn﴾ [Al 'Imran: 17]. If the seeking of forgiveness is within prayer, it is better. It has been established in the Sahih collections and others, from a group of the Companions, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed Allah descends every night to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains, and says: 'Is there anyone repentant that I may accept his repentance? Is there anyone seeking forgiveness that I may forgive him? Is there anyone asking that he may be given what he asks?' until dawn breaks." [Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih no. (758).]

[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (22/203), through the route of Sulayman al-Dimashqi, from 'Uthman ibn Fayid, from 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar, from al-Hirmas, raised to the Prophet with it. 'A'ishah, the Mother of the Believers, said: He is the destitute whose livelihood is hardly made easy for him. Al-Dahhak said: He is the one who has no wealth except that it is lost, and Allah decrees that for him.

Abu Qilabah said: A flood came in Yamamah and took the wealth of a man. A man among the Companions said: "This is the deprived one."

Ibn 'Abbas also said, and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Nafi' (the freedman of Ibn 'Umar), and 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: ﴿the deprived﴾ is the destitute (al-mahareef).

Qatadah and al-Zuhri said: ﴿the deprived﴾ is the one who does not ask people for anything. Al-Zuhri said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The needy one is not the one who goes around and is turned away by a morsel or two, or a date or two. Rather, the needy one is the one who does not find sufficient wealth to suffice him, and is not noticed so that he may be given charity."

This hadith has been transmitted by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) in their Sahihs through another route. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4539) and Sahih Muslim no. (1039), through Sharik ibn 'Abdullah, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, raised to the Prophet.]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: He is the one who comes after the spoils have been divided, and is given a small share.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: One of our companions narrated to me, saying: "We were with 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz on the road to Makkah, when a dog came, and 'Umar snatched a shoulder of a sheep and threw it to him, and said: 'They say that he is the deprived one.'"

Al-Sha'bi said: "I was unable to know what the deprived one is."

Imam Ahmad and a group of scholars held that hospitality to a guest is obligatory, and the Sunnah has reported this, as the apparent meaning of the revelation indicates.

* *

His saying, ﴿They said, "Peace." He said, "Peace."﴾: the nominative (ar-raf') is stronger and more established than the accusative (an-nasb), so returning the greeting in the nominative is better than merely greeting. For this reason the Exalted said: ﴿When you are greeted with a greeting, respond with one better than it, or return it﴾ [An-Nisa: 86]. Thus the Khalil (the Friend of Allah) chose the better option.

* *

His saying, ﴿Unknown people﴾: this is because the angels, who were Jibril, Israfil and Mika'il, came to him in the forms of handsome young men who bore great awe. For this reason he said, ﴿Unknown people.﴾

* *

His saying, ﴿He turned quickly to his family﴾: that is, he slipped away secretly and swiftly. ﴿Then he brought a fat calf﴾: that is, from the best of his wealth. In the other verse: ﴿He did not delay before bringing a roasted calf﴾ [Hud: 69], that is, one roasted on heated stones (al-radf). ﴿Then he set it before them﴾: that is, he brought it near to them. ﴿He said, "Will you not eat?"﴾: this is gentleness in speech and a gracious offer.

This verse contains the etiquette of hospitality. He brought his food swiftly and discreetly, without them noticing, and did not first impose on them by saying, "Shall we bring you food?" Rather, he brought it quickly and quietly, and he brought the best he found of his wealth, a young, fat, roasted calf. He set it before them and did not merely leave it aside, nor did he say, "Come forward." Rather, he placed it in front of them. He did not command them with a firm form of speech that would burden the listener. Instead he said, ﴿Will you not eat?﴾ as a gentle and courteous offer, just as a person today might say, "If you would be so kind, and would be generous and give charity, then do so" [Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, has expanded on the etiquette of hospitality in these verses in his book "Jala' al-Afham" (pp. 181–184)].

* *

They said, "Do not fear. We have been sent to the people of Lut." And his wife was standing, and she laughed﴾ [Hud: 70–71], that is, she rejoiced at their destruction because of their rebellion and defiance against Allah. At that point the angels gave her glad tidings of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub. ﴿She said, "Woe to me! Shall I bear a child when I am an old woman and this is my husband, an old man? Indeed, this is an amazing thing." They said, "Do you wonder at the decree of Allah? The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O people of the house. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Glorious"﴾ [Hud: 72–73]. For this reason He says here: ﴿And they gave him glad tidings of a knowing boy﴾. The glad tidings given to him were also glad tidings to her, because the child was from both of them, so each of them was given the glad tidings.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So We seized him and his hosts and cast them into the sea﴾, meaning We threw them into the yam (the sea), which is the ocean. ﴿And he was blameworthy﴾, meaning he was deserving of blame: a disbeliever, a denier, a wicked and obstinate transgressor.

Then He said: ﴿And in 'Ad, when We sent upon them the barren wind﴾, meaning the destructive wind that produces nothing. This was said by al-Dahhak, Qatadah and others.

For this reason He said: ﴿It left nothing it came upon without making it like what is crumbled to dust﴾, meaning like something perished and decayed, of what the wind destroyed.

Ibn Abi Hatim has said: Abu 'Ubaid Allah, the nephew of Ibn Wahb, narrated to us; my paternal uncle 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us; 'Abd Allah — meaning Ibn 'Ayyash [in M: "Ibn Abbas"] — al-Qutbani narrated to me; 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman narrated to me, from Darraj, from 'Isa ibn Hilal al-Sadafi, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The wind is subjected from the second [heaven] — meaning from the second earth. Ibn Kathir said, alerting to the creation of the upper and lower worlds: "And the heaven, We constructed it [with might]" (Qur'an 51:47), meaning: We made it a raised ceiling [preserved]. "With hands" means: with strength. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Thawri, and others. "And indeed, We are expanding it" means: We have widened its expanses and raised it without pillars, until it stood firm as it is.

"And the earth, We spread it out" (51:48) means: We made it a bed for the creatures. "How excellent are the ones who spread it out" means: We made it a cradle for its inhabitants.

"And of all things We created pairs" (51:49) means: all created things come in pairs: heaven and earth, night and day, sun and moon, land and sea, light and darkness, faith and disbelief, death and life, misery and happiness, Paradise and Fire, and even animals [jinn and humans, males and females] and plants. For this reason He said: "So that you may remember" (51:49), meaning: that you may know that the Creator is one, with no partner.

"So flee to Allah" (51:50), meaning: take refuge in Him and rely upon Him in your affairs. "Indeed, I am a clear warner to you from Him" (51:50).

"And do not set up with Allah another god" (51:51), meaning: [and] do not associate anything with Him. "Indeed, I am a clear warner to you from Him" (51:51).
